title: Tuna Pasta Bake
subtitle: A comforting pasta bake with a cheesy white sauce
excerpt: This is a proper baked pasta dish built on a proper white sauce, not a jar. Tuna, mushrooms, and peas go through the sauce before everything is topped with cheddar and baked until bubbling.
sourceNotes: Pasta bake became a staple of British family cooking in the 1970s and 1980s as dried pasta became widely available in supermarkets. The combination of tinned tuna and white sauce is a particular British comfort food classic.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before baking. Cover and freeze for up to 2 months. Bake from frozen at 180C for 45 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Assemble in two dishes and freeze one unbaked.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to a day ahead. Cover and refrigerate. Add 10 minutes to the bake time.

content.text: Keep stirring the white sauce from the moment the milk goes in. A few seconds without attention is enough for the bottom to catch and turn lumpy.

items.prepNote: grated, 100g for sauce and 50g for topping

content.text: Cook the pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Drain and set aside.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan over a medium heat.
Add the mushrooms. Cook for 5 minutes until softened. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, melt the remaining butter over a medium heat.
Add the flour. Stir and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the milk gradually, whisking constantly.
Cook over a medium heat, stirring, for 5 to 6 minutes until the sauce is thick and smooth.
Remove from the heat. Stir in 100g of the cheddar. Season well.
Add the pasta, mushrooms, tuna, and peas. Fold gently to combine.
Transfer to a large baking dish. Scatter the remaining cheddar over the top.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until bubbling and golden on top.

items.cause: Milk added too fast or not stirred constantly.
items.fix: Whisk vigorously. For stubborn lumps, push through a sieve.

items.cause: Pasta was fully cooked before going into the dish.
items.fix: Always undercook the pasta by 2 minutes before baking.

items.cause: Too little cheese or oven not hot enough.
items.fix: Grill for the last 3 minutes to get a golden crust.
